clue.text: Marries and goes off embracing husband after speculation

indicators.note: after places the speculation piece before the rest in the answer... read as the rest coming after it

parts.note: a bet is a speculation on an outcome

indicators.note: embracing means one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: food that goes off rots

explanation.surface: Someone weds and then wanders off with a husband after a gamble, a racy little story.
explanation.definitionFit: To betroth is to promise in marriage, so it stands loosely for marries, its transitive verb sense matching.

clue.text: Protection from weather? British happy to forgo headpiece

indicators.note: to forgo headpiece means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: jolly means happy

explanation.surface: Seeking cover from the rain, a cheerful Briton goes without a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A brolly is British slang for an umbrella, which shields its holder from rain.

clue.text: Row about component of education for painstaking student?

indicators.note: about means the row goes round the other piece

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic, are the basics of education, so R is one part

explanation.surface: A quarrel over the school curriculum, raised on behalf of a diligent pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel, but it is a line of seats. The question mark marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A painstaking student is one who makes a real effort, someone who keeps attempting things.

clue.text: Some deliveries friend picked up showing a degree of duplication

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries bowled

indicators.note: picked up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom up, reversed

parts.note: a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: a bowler's mate catches some balls, showing the work is repeated.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls bowled by one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: An overlap is where two things cover some of the same ground, a partial duplication.

clue.text: Pair of lines showing Batman and Robin possibly appearing on time

parts.note: the comic-book crime fighters are an example of a brave pair

explanation.surface: A comic-strip duo turns up on schedule, as two lines of dialogue.
explanation.definitionFit: A heroic couplet is a pair of rhyming iambic pentameter lines, as used by Pope and Dryden.

clue.text: Confused chatter about river fish

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: Babel is a confused noise of many voices, after the tower in Genesis

explanation.surface: Muddled talk about a river fish, as if anglers were gossiping.
explanation.definitionFit: The barbel is a freshwater fish of the carp family with whisker-like barbels by its mouth.

clue.text: Harmonised a duet not disregarding old fashions

indicators.note: fashions as a verb means shapes, so the remaining letters are reshaped
disregarding means the old letter is ignored and left out

explanation.surface: Two singers bring their duet into tune while keeping up with outdated styles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashions' looks like a noun about style, but it is a verb: the letters left after 'disregarding' drops O are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Attuned means brought into harmony or tuned to agree, a synonym of harmonised.

clue.text: Area for sales and storage beside the rink?

parts.note: a box is a container for storage
off the ice is next to the skating rink

explanation.surface: A sports arena's layout: a sales point and a storeroom alongside the skating rink.
explanation.definitionFit: The box office is where tickets are sold at a theatre or venue.

clue.text: Boy with disgusted comment about large fortune

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: about means the disgusted exclamation goes round the other piece

parts.note: yuck is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: A boy turns his nose up at a large sum of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Luck is fortune personified as a woman, the force that gives chance outcomes.

clue.text: Uniform material was adopted by soldiers and sailor

indicators.note: adopted by means taken in by the soldiers piece, so it sits inside it

parts.note: OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers
to have lived is to have existed, to have been
AB is an able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: A cloth was taken up by the army and navy, a quartermaster's report.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive drab is the dull greenish khaki cloth used for military uniforms, notably by the US Army.

clue.text: Preserves narrow strip of land containing core of some abundant resource

indicators.note: containing means the preserves word holds the middle letters inside it

parts.note: to bottle fruit is to preserve it

indicators.note: core of means the middle letters of the word some

parts.note: a spit is a narrow point of land running into the sea

explanation.surface: A cook's tale: jars of preserves on a sandbar, filled from some generous supply.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottomless pit is a source that never runs dry, an inexhaustible supply.

clue.text: Moved to take-off after disembarking one becoming stressed

indicators.note: disembarking means the one gets off, taken out of the word

parts.note: an aircraft taxied, moving along the runway towards take-off
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An aeroplane's journey to the runway, with a passenger getting off and growing tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Taxed in the sense of strained or burdened is a close synonym of stressed.

clue.text: Legend of river and lake that is put back beside other legends

parts.note: lore is a body of traditional tales and legends

indicators.note: put back means the letters for that is are reversed

parts.note: i.e. (id est) means that is

explanation.surface: A folklore survey: tales of a river and a lake set beside other myths.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole phrase 'Legend of river': the Lorelei is the siren of the Rhine.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lorelei is the German legend of a siren on a Rhine rock who lured boatmen to their doom.

clue.text: Ravel's one enthralled by flute playing of melodious quality

indicators.note: enthralled by means held inside the reworked letters
playing means the letters of flute are performed in a new order

parts.note: Ravel was French, and un is French for one

explanation.surface: A piece by Ravel features a captivating flute part with a sweet melodic character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ravel's' suggests the composer's music, but here it only signals that the word for one is French.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tuneful has a pleasant melody, the quality the definition describes.

clue.text: One lacking complaint nevertheless inclined to be patient

definitions.text: One lacking complaint nevertheless inclined to be patient

parts.words: One lacking complaint nevertheless inclined to be patient
parts.note: someone with no illness who still keeps casting themselves as a patient under medical care

explanation.surface: A person with no ailment who still behaves as though under a doctor's care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patient' looks like the adjective meaning tolerant, but it is the noun: someone receiving treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who constantly imagines being ill without any real disease is exactly what the clue describes.

clue.text: Cleanliness expert — sadly in pig-sty he has no power

indicators.note: sadly means the letters are in a sorry state, mixed up
has no means the power letter is taken away

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A hygiene expert stuck in a pigsty is powerless to do anything about the mess.
explanation.definitionFit: A hygienist specialises in cleanliness and health, as a dental hygienist does with teeth.

clue.text: Big store I line up with little hesitation, raking millions in

indicators.note: raking, with in, means collecting the millions inside
in completes raking in, so the millions letter goes within
up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: a rope is a line, as on a ship
um is a brief sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper falls into line with little hesitation, raking in millions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses I and ROPE to EPORI, and 'raking ... in' puts M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An emporium is a large shop or department store selling many kinds of goods.

clue.text: Game UCD alumna put out degree citation

indicators.note: put out means disturbed or disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A graduate of University College Dublin who loves sport is upset by something.
explanation.definitionFit: Magna cum laude, Latin for with great praise, is a distinction printed on a university degree.

clue.text: Condition I intend escalating among reforming drinkers

indicators.note: among means set inside the other piece

parts.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous, the group for drinkers trying to reform

indicators.note: escalating means rising, so in a down clue the letters are reversed

parts.note: to mean to do something is to intend it

explanation.surface: A recovering alcoholic plans to tackle a worsening medical condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'escalating' reverses I MEAN to NAEMI, which goes 'among' the AA.
explanation.definitionFit: Anaemia is a medical condition marked by too few red blood cells.

clue.text: Old soldier cut down after rifleman missed first alarm

indicators.note: after puts the cut-down old soldier behind the rifleman piece
missed first means the first letter is lost

parts.note: a gunner is someone who fires a gun

indicators.note: cut down means the word is shortened by its last letter

parts.note: a vet is a veteran, an old soldier

explanation.surface: A veteran soldier is struck down after a rifleman misses with the first shot.
explanation.definitionFit: To unnerve someone is to make them lose courage, which is to frighten or alarm them.

clue.text: Favourite part in brief? It's refined stuff

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as the teacher's pet

indicators.note: brief means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a role is a part in a play

explanation.surface: An actor's favourite part in a short play turns out to be a classy affair.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrol is fuel produced by refining crude oil, so it is a refined substance.

clue.text: Finished a couple of lengths in total

parts.note: something finished is over
L is the abbreviation for length, so two of them make LL

explanation.surface: A race report: someone finished a couple of lengths ahead overall.
explanation.definitionFit: Overall used as an adverb means taken as a whole, synonymous with altogether.

clue.text: Cautious about soldier perhaps in US city

indicators.note: about means the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: playing it safe is being cautious
a soldier is a type of ant, so an ant is an example

explanation.surface: A wary soldier stationed in some American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa Fe is the state capital of New Mexico in the United States.

clue.text: Whiskey consumed by a military group in former days

indicators.note: consumed by means swallowed inside the military group

parts.note: the SAS is the Special Air Service, a British army regiment
W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A regiment downs whisky, as soldiers did in years gone by.
explanation.definitionFit: As was is a phrase meaning as it used to be, describing how something was previously.

clue.text: I'd recalled way of working one part of speech

parts.note: I'd written without its apostrophe

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the following letters are read backwards

parts.note: MO is modus operandi, a way of working
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone remembers a method that worked for a single bit of grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a fixed expression used in a language, so a piece of its speech.

clue.text: Leading attraction? The Queen, among the aristocracy

parts.note: a top draw is the main attraction that pulls in a crowd
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Royalty is the star turn at a gathering of the nobility.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-drawer means of the highest social class, so describes someone belonging to the upper crust.

clue.text: Fall back, displacing new line in reciprocal arrangement

indicators.note: displacing means the line pushes out the new, which is dropped
back means the season word is reversed

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: Two parties fall back into a give-and-take deal after a change of line.
explanation.walkthrough: AUTUMN reversed is NMUTUA; 'displacing' removes N and L takes its role at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutual agreement is one shared and returned by both parties, which is reciprocal.

clue.text: Results after cooking will include ultimate in apple crumble

indicators.note: will include means the reworked letters take the last letter inside them
after cooking means the letters of results are mixed up as if cooked
ultimate in means the last letter of the word apple

explanation.surface: A baking note: what comes out of the oven will include an apple crumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after cooking' rearranges RESULTS, and 'will include' puts E, the last letter of 'apple', inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Streusel is a crumbly topping of flour, butter and sugar, a crumble used on cakes and pies.
